title: ID0428673-DC/Si-D/BE[170001921] - Charging issue
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
EV charging properly when limited to max SoC 80% but acts different when limit is raised to 90% or 100%
Root cause: EV is stopping the session - reason unclear. Needs .pcap files, EcoG 1.4.12 installed.
Solution:
Install EcoG 1.4.12

additional_info.subject: ID0428673-DC/Si-D/BE[170001921] - Charging issue CRM:00315002704
additional_info.body:
Hi Chlöe,
Thank you very much for the timestamp, it helped a lot.
Here are my findings, please be aware that the time shown is according to UTC so -2h from your location.
Here is the Start charging log for the session that ended early:
(From bottom to top)
We were charging at ~93kW when we could reach 140kW (EV didn't require more than 93kW), and the Target Current (requested by EV) is being supplied correctly by us (Now Current), there is always a difference of a few Amps, as you can see 1A.
But then you can see the current being dropped by the EV, slowly ramping down and going to 0A.
The second session which works better:
If the EV charges properly when limited to 80% SoC why wouldn't it be able to charge with a different limit? This definitely looks like an EV issue.
What kind of EV is it and model?
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0428673-DC/Si-D/BE[170001921] - Charging issue CRM:00315002704
additional_info.body:
Hi Chlöe,
Thanks for the feedback.
For us to completely understand what went wrong, I would require the following:
Install the 1.4.11 version of the SECC which has a extra layer of logs called V2G. This is the communication exchanged between Charger and EV. This does not affect the performance of the charger.
Perform a session with the EV and refer back to us as soon as possible since these logs are overwritten depending on the number of sessions performed.
Please let me know if this suits you and if you want to schedule a remote session, we can also support.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
